holidays.name: Mickey Mouse Birthday (Mickey's Birthday)
holidays.description: Fans around the world celebrate the debut of the world's most famous mouse, with ear-wearing, cartoon marathons, and a lot of whistling.
holidays.origin: Mickey Mouse's official birthday is November 18, 1928, the date Steamboat Willie premiered at the Colony Theater in New York City. It was the first widely distributed cartoon with synchronized sound, though Mickey had appeared in earlier test shorts.
holidays.funFact: Walt Disney originally wanted to name the character Mortimer Mouse, but his wife Lillian reportedly said it sounded too pompous and suggested Mickey instead.

holidays.name: Occult Day
holidays.description: A day for embracing the mysterious, with tarot readings, candle rituals, and conversations about the strange and hidden corners of human belief.
holidays.origin: Occult Day is an unofficial observance of recent origin, tied to the idea that the occult means 'hidden' in Latin (occultus). It encourages curiosity about esoteric knowledge, folklore, and mystical traditions.
holidays.funFact: The word 'occult' comes from the Latin 'occultus,' meaning 'secret' or 'hidden,' and was once used in science to describe things like hidden or unexplained forces.

holidays.name: Push Button Phone Day
holidays.description: A salute to the dial-less telephone that freed us from the agony of waiting for the rotary wheel to spin all the way back after dialing a 9.
holidays.origin: The first commercial push-button telephone was introduced by Bell Telephone on November 18, 1963, in Carnegie and Greensburg, Pennsylvania, using Touch-Tone technology.
holidays.funFact: Early Touch-Tone phone designers tested many button layouts, including a circular one, before settling on the familiar 3x4 grid we still use today.

holidays.name: National Princess Day
holidays.description: A day for dressing up in tiaras, hosting tea parties, and celebrating princesses of all kinds, real or fictional, regal or royally sassy.
holidays.origin: National Princess Day is a modern unofficial observance popular with children and parents, often connected to fairy tales and animated movies. It encourages kindness, confidence, and a bit of dress-up fun.
holidays.funFact: Many classic fairy tale princesses, such as Cinderella, have hundreds of versions worldwide, with the oldest known Cinderella-style story dating back to ancient Greece or Egypt.

holidays.name: National Vichyssoise Day
holidays.description: A chilly celebration of the creamy potato and leek soup that is traditionally served cold, which is a bold choice for a November evening.
holidays.origin: Vichyssoise is generally credited to chef Louis Diat of the Ritz-Carlton in New York City, who created his version in 1917 based on his mother's hot potato and leek soup from his childhood in France.
holidays.funFact: Despite its French-sounding name, vichyssoise is considered by many to be an American invention, and Diat said he chilled the soup by adding cold milk to cool it for his brother.
